claude.sample_unit: patient questions (each run under 3 prompt conditions in 2 LLMs)

links.outcome: Reading grade level of LLM responses with vs without prompt specifying grade level
links.effect: Average grade reading level 13.45 (stand-alone), 11.5 (prompt A), 10.3 (prompt B) (p < 0.001); prompt B lowered accuracy and comprehensiveness (median 4.0 vs 5.0).
links.quote: Average-grade reading level of responses across both LLMs were 13.45, 11.5, and 10.3 for a stand-alone question, prompt A, and prompt B questions, respectively (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Readability, accuracy and comprehensiveness of LLM patient education responses under prompt engineering
links.effect: Prompt engineering improved readability (grade 13.45 to 10.3) but prompt B reduced accuracy and comprehensiveness (median 4.0 vs 5.0, p < 0.001).
links.quote: Prompt engineering can significantly improve readability of LLM-generated responses, although at the cost of reducing accuracy and comprehensiveness.

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering with optimized prompts and reading-level/length constraints to improve LLM patient education responses

links.effect: Grade level fell from 13.45 to 10.3 (p < 0.001), but prompt B median accuracy and comprehensiveness fell from 5.0 to 4.0.
links.quote: Prompt engineering can significantly improve readability of LLM-generated responses, although at the cost of reducing accuracy and comprehensiveness.

links.effect: Median accuracy was 5.0, 5.0, 4.0 and comprehensiveness 5.0, 5.0, 4.0 for stand-alone, prompt A, prompt B; prompt B lower (p < 0.001).
links.quote: The use of prompt B was associated with a lower accuracy and comprehensiveness than responses to stand-alone question or prompt A questions (p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Using optimized prompts for LLM-generated patient education responses on retinal diseases
